archetypes.name: Metronome
archetypes.blurb: Holds within a couple of percent of its own average pace almost all the way.

archetypes.name: Gentle fader
archetypes.blurb: A little quicker than average early, a little slower late. The most common shape.

archetypes.name: Late fader
archetypes.blurb: Holds a brisk pace to about 25 km, then gives most of it back over 30–40 km.

archetypes.name: Early drifter
archetypes.blurb: Starts quick and slows in every section from 10 km on, slowest over 30–35 km, then eases slightly at the end.

archetypes.name: Cliff
archetypes.blurb: Holds a fast pace to 25 km, then the 35–40 km section is about 40% slower than average.

archetypes.name: Fast-start fader
archetypes.blurb: Very quick for 15 km, with the steepest slowing between 25 and 35 km.

classifier.rule: r_i = 100*(section pace / whole-race average pace - 1); x_i = clip(r_i, lo_i, hi_i) * sqrt(km_i / 5); archetype = nearest centroid

method: Relative pace compares each recorded section with the same finish's whole-race average pace. Profiles are clipped at the 0.1st and 99.9th percentiles, weighted by section length and grouped by k-means into six landmarks, then named by rules: least late slowing is the Metronome, the next is the Gentle fader, and within the two stronger pairs the one that slows earlier is the Early drifter or Fast-start fader. Left out of these shape statistics: 15 editions whose first 5 km appears to include start delay. Repeat pairs use screened identity candidates with one finish in each of two years at most three years apart; they are not verified people.
